results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around The Jolly Balloon Man, Sewer-veillance Cam and Bloom Tender.
results.text:
I built a four-color Craterhoof ramp brew (green, white, blue, red) around your three cards. It uses the mana and threats of the Aang deck, which is the strategy that already plays both Bloom Tender and Sewer-veillance Cam. It's legal, 60 cards with a 15-card sideboard, and passed the deck check with no warnings.

**The plan:** Bloom Tender makes one mana of each color among your permanents. With Bloom Tender (green), The Jolly Balloon Man (red and white) and Sewer-veillance Cam (blue) on the board, it makes 4 mana per tap. The Jolly Balloon Man pays {1} and taps to make a token copy of Bloom Tender. The copy has haste, so it taps right away for 4 more mana. The Cam can come in at instant speed to untap Bloom Tender for another 4, and when you sacrifice it later it untaps something again and draws two cards. One big turn like that pays for Craterhoof Behemoth (8 mana), or Nature's Rhythm can fetch it. On a later turn, The Jolly Balloon Man copies Craterhoof, and the copy's haste means it triggers a second "+X/+X and trample to everything" for a lethal attack.

**How I chose this direction:**
- **Option A (picked):** the Aang/Craterhoof ramp package from your list: Llanowar Elves, Gene Pollinator, Ouroboroid, Brightglass Gearhulk, Nature's Rhythm, Craterhoof Behemoth.
- **Option B:** a white-blue-red deck where The Jolly Balloon Man copies creatures with enter-the-battlefield effects, like Glamermite and Aang.
- **Option C:** a green-blue Formidable Speaker untap engine.

I picked A because it's the only one where all three cards do real work. Bloom Tender's mana is what the ramp needs, The Jolly Balloon Man doubles both the mana and the finisher, and Brightglass Gearhulk can fetch the Cam.

**Things to know:**
- **There's no infinite combo here.** I checked every card in Standard with an "untap" ability (Glamermite, Flash Thompson, North Pole Patrol, Formidable Speaker). None of them untaps The Jolly Balloon Man more than once per copy it pays for. This deck is a big burst of mana, not a loop.
- **Badgermole Cub is now banned.** The Aang lists still play it, so it isn't in this deck. Spider Manifestation fills that slot as a red/green mana creature.
- **Odds:** you have about a 53% chance to draw any single 4-of by turn 4, and only about 27% to draw both Bloom Tender and The Jolly Balloon Man. Nature's Rhythm fills the gaps: X=2 finds Tender and X=3 finds The Jolly Balloon Man. Brightglass Gearhulk can fetch the Cam or more mana creatures.
- The deck check rated the exact turn-5 sequence at about 1% of games, because that counts drawing every card in it naturally. Realistically, expect to win around turns 5–6 when the pieces come together. The mana base is 22 lands based on what four-color decks in these colors play: shocklands, Starting Town, Multiversal Passage and Hushwood Verge.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Dáin's Company, Dwarven Mauler and Kíli the Resourceful.
results.text:
I built **Boros Dwarves Equipment**, a low-curve brew for Standard (average mana value 1.76).

**Plan:** Play a Dwarf every turn, starting with a turn-1 Dwarven Mauler. Put cheap Equipment on your creatures. Mauler's discount makes Lavaspur Boots free to equip and drops Dwarven Mattock's equip from {3} to {1}. Kíli draws a card each turn a Dwarf or Equipment enters (once per turn), and Dáin's Company digs four cards deep for whichever piece you're missing.

Kíli turns on "storied" once you control three artifacts and/or legendaries. Then your first equip each turn costs nothing, so a 3-mana Mattock equip becomes free. The deck has 14 legendaries plus 8 Equipment, so you usually reach this by turn 3. The finisher is Dáin Ironfoot: when he attacks, every equipped attacker gains double strike. A Mauler wearing Mattock and Boots then hits for 10.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Pure Dwarves plus Equipment, using the burn package from Boros Aggro (Burst Lightning).** This is the one I picked.
2. **Building on the Boros Weapons shell from the meta list.** Despite the name, that deck is about artifact tokens and Weapons Manufacturing, not equipping creatures. It would have left your three cards with nothing to do.
3. **A heavier build around Dáin Ironfoot and Thorin, Mountain-king.** Too slow against Prowess, which is 22% of the field.

I chose option 1 because all three of your cards reward one cheap density of Dwarves and Equipment. It has 26 Dwarves and 8 Equipment, so Company almost always finds a hit and Kíli draws nearly every turn.

**Notes:**
- **How often it comes together:** You'll have Kíli or Company by turn 3 about 75% of the time, Equipment about 75% of the time, and both together 55% of the time.
- **The full win line is not the normal plan.** The checker says you'll draw that exact sequence by turn 5 in only 0.1% of games. Most wins will come from the same idea with different pieces: Giott's double strike, Fíli's +1/+1 to the team, or Thorin Oakenshield giving everything ward 1.
- **These cards are untested.** None of the Dwarf cards show up in tournament results from the last 90 days, so treat this as a first draft.
- **Mana and sideboard:** The 22 lands come from what real Boros decks play. I added 2 The Lonely Mountain, which makes 2/2 Dwarves late in the game. The sideboard is aimed at the decks in your meta snapshot: Sear and Abrade against Prowess and Elementals, Ghost Vacuum and Rest in Peace against Lessons and Reanimator, Magebane Lizard against spell-heavy decks, and Shattered Acolyte (itself a Dwarf) against artifacts and enchantments.

Clears blockers or deals the last 2 to 4 damage

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Greedy Freebooter, The Sackville-Bagginses and Umbral Collar Zealot.
results.text:
I built an Orzhov (white-black) aristocrats deck: it makes creatures and tokens, sacrifices them, and drains the opponent each time. I'm calling it a brew because no published list in the last 400 days plays your three cards together, so there was no existing deck to start from.

**How it plays.** Greedy Freebooter, Infestation Sage and Bloodghast are cheap creatures to sacrifice. Freebooter leaves a Treasure when it dies, Sage leaves a 1/1 flying Insect, and Bloodghast comes back from the graveyard whenever you play a land. Umbral Collar Zealot lets you sacrifice a creature or artifact at any time for free. The Sackville-Bagginses eats one of those creatures when it enters to draw a card and make a Treasure. After that, every token you sacrifice makes the opponent lose 1 life. Popular Egotist, Vito and Sephiroth turn each sacrifice into more drain, and Vito makes a 4/3 flier on the third sacrifice in a turn.

**Sample win, around turn 6:**
1. Turn 1: Freebooter.
2. Turn 2: Zealot.
3. Turn 3: Sackville, sacrificing Freebooter. That gives you a card and two Treasures.
4. Turn 4: Vito, cast with help from a Treasure. Sacrifice things to Zealot: the first gains you 2 life, the second drains 2 and Vito's third makes the 4/3 flier. Sackville adds 1 drain for each Treasure.
5. Egotist adds another point of drain on every sacrifice to close out the game.

Drawing that exact set of cards by turn 6 is rare (about 2%). The deck works through redundancy instead. You have at least one sacrifice outlet by turn 3 in about 94% of games and a cheap creature to sacrifice in about 91%, with both together about 85% of the time.

**Directions I considered:**
- **Rakdos (black-red), using Mardu Discard's Bloodghast package:** I dropped it because only 5 recent black-red lists exist and there was no drain payoff as strong as Vito.
- **Golgari (black-green) Food:** It has Experimental Confectioner and Scavenger's Talent, but most of their triggers care about Food, not the Treasures your cards make.
- **Orzhov, using the Lifegain deck's mana and removal (chosen):** Tolls of War, Vito and Ruthless Lawbringer add a second layer of sacrifice payoffs. The lands come from the 73 recent white-black lists, almost all of them Lifegain.

**Other choices:**
- **Removal:** Erode, Requiting Hex and Bitter Triumph are all widely played. Requiting Hex has a small trick: you can put its -1/-1 counter on your own Freebooter, which kills it and gives you a Treasure.
- **Fountainport:** I added one copy. It can sacrifice a token to draw a card, which also triggers Sackville's drain.
- **Sideboard:** It's aimed at the top decks in the field: Prowess, Landfall, Dimir Excruciator, Reanimator and Mardu Discard.

The deck passed the legality and mana checks with no warnings. Its land count and colored sources line up with real white-black Lifegain lists.

**Main deck (60)**

- 3 Infestation Sage
- 4 Umbral Collar Zealot
- 3 The Sackville-Bagginses
- 3 Bloodghast
- 4 Popular Egotist
- 2 Sephiroth, Fabled SOLDIER
- 2 Ruthless Lawbringer

- 3 Tolls of War
- 3 Erode
- 2 Requiting Hex
- 2 Bitter Triumph
- 4 Godless Shrine
- 4 Concealed Courtyard
- 2 Bleachbone Verge
- 3 Shattered Sanctum
- 2 Starting Town
- 1 Fountainport
- 4 Swamp
- 2 Plains

**Sideboard (15)**
- 2 Duress
- 2 Strategic Betrayal
- 2 Leyline of the Void
- 2 Seam Rip
- 2 Pyrrhic Strike
- 2 Deep-Cavern Bat
- 1 Ancient Vendetta
- 2 Shoot the Sheriff

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Gideon's Memorial, Solitary Cell and Ajani Unrelenting.
results.text:
I built **Boros Superfriends Tokens**, a brew for Standard. No published list in the last 400 days plays all three of your cards together, so there was no proven shell to start from.

**The plan:** You make creature tokens with Hop to It, Elspeth, Storm Slayer and Ajani, Outland Chaperone. Gideon's Memorial gives those tokens +1/+0 and vigilance, so they can attack and still guard your planeswalkers. The Memorial also taps for any color to cast planeswalkers, so it works as a mana rock that gets Chandra, Torch of Defiance out early and Ajani Unrelenting out a turn or two sooner. Ajani's −3 deals 4 damage to every creature except your tokens, which makes it a one-sided board wipe. It also creates a Cadet token (two with Elspeth out). The next turn, its +1 gives your tokens haste and +1/+0 for the finishing attack. Solitary Cell removes an early threat costing 3 or less. Late in the game it turns extra Memorials or walkers into new cards: 16 of the 60 cards are legendary and can be discarded to it.

**Three directions I considered:**
1. **Go-wide Boros Aggro** using the Voice of Victory and Song of Totentanz shell. Ajani costs 6, which is too expensive for that curve.
2. **Jeskai control** using the Azorius package of No More Lies and Day of Judgment. Day of Judgment kills your own tokens and works against Ajani's one-sided wipe.
3. **Boros Superfriends Tokens.** I chose this one because all three of your cards have a job in it: the Memorial for mana and the anthem, the Cell for removal and card draw, and Ajani as the wipe and finisher. It borrows Hop to It, Warleader's Call and the mana base from Boros Aggro, the closest proven deck.

**Numbers to know:**
- 23 lands, which matches what Boros decks run. Cavern of Souls is left out because the deck has no creature spells.
- By turn 5 you'll have a token maker in 89% of games and a Memorial in 57%.
- The full win line ends on turn 7. Drawing every exact card in it by then happens only about 3% of the time. In practice the deck has backups for each step: 12 walkers, 4 Hop to It and 11 removal spells.

The 15-card sideboard is aimed at the current top decks:
- **Rest in Peace** for Reanimator and Jund Sacrifice
- **Sear, Seam Rip and Slagstorm** for Elementals, Prowess and Landfall
- **Dawn's Truce** to protect your walkers from Dimir's removal

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Jeskai Revelation, Inevitable Defeat and Tablet of Discovery.
results.text:
This is a 4-color control brew (Jeskai base with a black splash), and the checker accepted it. You counter and remove threats early, then win with your requested cards. Tablet of Discovery's RR (only for instants and sorceries) lets you cast Jeskai Revelation a turn early, around five lands plus Tablet. Inevitable Defeat exiles their best permanent, can't be countered, and drains 3. Each Revelation is worth about five cards: it bounces a threat, deals 4 to any target, makes two prowess Monks, draws two and gains 4 life. The Wandering Emperor and the burn finish the game from there.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **4-color control (chosen).** In the data I looked at, all three cards show up together only in Standard 4C Control lists (135 of them). I ported that deck and filled it with the Pioneer UW Control package from your menu: No More Lies, Get Lost, Supreme Verdict, Consult the Star Charts, Stock Up and The Wandering Emperor.
2. **Jeskai spells/Lessons.** This would use Tablet as a spell engine, but it leaves out black, so it can't cast Inevitable Defeat.
3. **Niv-Mizzet-style 5-color.** Those decks win with their own big ramp package, so your three cards would be passengers.

I picked direction 1 because it's the only one where all three cards do real work, and the Standard results back it up.

**How the deck is built:**
- **Black sources:** 10 lands make black, which is enough to cast Inevitable Defeat on turn 4 or 5.
- **Mana base:** No real Pioneer decks run these exact colors yet, so I built the 25 lands myself from shocklands, triomes, Verges and Mana Confluence. That's 18 white sources and 16 each for blue and red, plus the 4 Tablets.
- **The one rare card:** The checker flagged Sear because almost no Pioneer decks play it. I kept it because it kills Sheoldred, Screaming Nemesis and Greasefang at instant speed. Fatal Push, the usual pick, needs black on turns 1–2, which a splash can't give reliably.

**Caveats:**
- The win line I entered lists six specific cards, and you'll have drawn all six by turn 9 in only about 2% of games. That number is misleading: you don't need all six, since any mix of counters, removal, Revelation and Defeat gets you to the same endgame. Still, expect long games.
- Six triomes and tap lands make the deck slow, so fast Mono-Red Prowess is the toughest matchup.

**Sideboard:** It's aimed at the top decks in your menu. Rest in Peace is for Greasefang and Izzet Phoenix, Pyroclasm, Brotherhood's End and Beza for the prowess decks, and Mystical Dispute, extra Dovin's Vetoes and Narset for control and Lotus Field.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Tolarian Terror, Bushwhack and Eddymurk Crab.
results.text:
I built a Simic (blue-green) spells deck, and it's a brew. No published list in the last 400 days runs these three cards together. In fact, Tolarian Terror and Bushwhack show up in 0 Pioneer lists, and Eddymurk Crab shows up in just one (an Izzet Crab deck).

**The plan:** The deck plays 28 one- and two-mana instants and sorceries. Consider, Opt, Sleight of Hand and Bushwhack's "search for a basic land" mode fill your graveyard while you hit your land drops. Tolarian Terror and Eddymurk Crab cost 1 less for each instant or sorcery in your graveyard, so they come down for 1–3 mana around turn 3. Once you have a 5/5 out, Bushwhack, Tail Swipe and Decisive Denial stop being filler and become one- and two-mana removal by making your creature fight theirs. Eddymurk Crab has flash: cast it at the end of your opponent's turn, or cast it on your own turn to tap two of their blockers so your 5/5s get through for 10. Snakeskin Veil and Terror's ward 2 protect your threats until they win the game in about three attacks.

**Three directions I considered:**
1. **Straight Simic, with fight spells as removal.** This is the one I chose.
2. **Temur, adding red's Fiery Impulse and Prismari Charm** from the Izzet Crab and Izzet Phoenix lists. This was rejected: running three colors would cost the deck its cheap, reliable mana.
3. **Simic using the Lessons/Prowess cards** Stormchaser's Talent and Boomerang Basics.

I chose Simic because with the 5/5s, green's one-mana fight spells do the job red would have done, without a third color. I still took the best part of direction 3: Stormchaser's Talent gives you a turn-1 creature, and its level 2 returns a spent spell from your graveyard to your hand. Boomerang Basics can bounce a threat, or bounce your own Talent so you can recast it for another 1/1 token and draw a card.

**Things to know:**
- **Land count:** The deck plays 19 lands. The checker recommended about 24, but that number counts the 7-mana creatures at full cost, which you'll almost never pay. The Izzet Crab list also ran 19.
- **Mana:** There's no proven blue-green list to copy (the blue-green lists in the data are Lotus Field and Scapeshift decks, which work differently), so I built the mana myself: Breeding Pool, Botanical Sanctum, Pathways, Otawara and Boseiju. That gives 16 blue and 14 green sources.
- **Odds:** You'll see at least one of the 10 big creatures by turn 4 in about 86% of games, and one of the 9 fight spells in about 83%. You'll have both in about 71%.
- **The win line:** The checker says all five cards in my example line show up by turn 6 in only about 3% of games. That's because it's one exact sequence. In practice, any cantrip, any big creature and any fight spell play those roles.
- **Card choices:** The checker pointed out that Pioneer players pick Boomerang Basics far more often than Fading Hope, Tail Swipe or Decisive Denial. I swapped Fading Hope for Boomerang Basics. I kept Tail Swipe and Decisive Denial because next to a 5/5 they actually kill creatures. Decisive Denial can also counter a noncreature spell (unless they pay 3) against Greasefang and UW Control.
- **Sideboard:** Graveyard hate (Unlicensed Hearse and Tormod's Crypt) is for Greasefang. Aether Gust is for the red and green decks. Negate, Mystical Dispute and Disdainful Stroke are for control and Cauldron. Pick Your Poison answers Parhelion II and Unholy Annex.
